nodes.name: InteriorFOC_Neg
nodes.docstring:
**Interior first-order condition — negative branch.**

Under the same hypotheses as `Claim1_RuleOutInterior`, suppose furthermore
`lqNorm q (p_star - f) > 0` and `lqNorm q p_star > 0`. Then for every
index `j` with `σ j = -1` and `p_star j < 0`, the first-order condition
holds:
`(f j - p_star j)^(q-1) / (lqNorm q (p_star - f))^(q-1)
  = λ · (-(p_star j))^(q-1) / (lqNorm q p_star)^(q-1)`.

Paper reference: Block 2, Steps 2.3.1–2.3.4 (KKT negative branch);
mirror of `InteriorFOC_Pos` with sign flips.
nodes.rationale: First-order condition at an interior negative-branch coordinate (p_j<0): the partial derivative of g vanishes, (f_j-p_j)^{q-1}/||p-f||^{q-1} = lambda*(-p_j)^{q-1}/||p||^{q-1}. Exactly the p_j<0 line of the displayed FOC system in the proof of the local-optimal-condition lemma.

nodes.name: SignIncompatibility

**Sign Incompatibility lemma.**

Under the same hypotheses as `Claim1_RuleOutInterior`, with
`lqNorm q (p_star - f) > 0` and `lqNorm q p_star > 0`, the following two
conditions cannot both hold simultaneously:

* (P) there exists `j` with `σ j = +1`, `p_star j ≥ f j`, and `f j > 0`;
* (N) there exists `i` with `σ i = -1`, `p_star i < 0`, and `f i > 0`.

Paper reference: `approx.tex` lines 103–106; Block 4, Steps 4.1–4.3
(Gravin & Jia, *Approximation guarantees of Median Mechanism in ℝ^d*,
arXiv:2502.08578v2).

nodes.name: CG
nodes.docstring:
The closed-form consistency bound `CG(c)` for the `CMP(c)` mechanism at
`q = 2` (Euclidean L₂), from Theorem 3 of Gravin & Jia.

For `c < 1/2`:
`CG(c) = √(4·√(2c+3)·c + 6·√(2c+3) − 10c − 8) / (c + 1)`.

For `c ≥ 1/2`:
`CG(c) = √(2 / (c + 1))`.

(The `^{1/2}` in the paper is rendered with `Real.sqrt`.)
nodes.rationale: Closed-form consistency bound CG(c) from Theorem 3: the piecewise expression that is the RHS of consistency_guarantee.

nodes.name: augment
nodes.docstring:
The `CMP(c)`-augmented instance: the original `n` agent reports `P`
augmented with `k` copies of the prediction `pred`. Indices `< n` return the
corresponding original report `P i`; indices `≥ n` (the last `k`) return `pred`.

Modeling choice: the index split uses `Fin.addCases`, so for
`i : Fin (n + k)` the result is `P` on the `Fin n` summand and the constant
`pred` on the `Fin k` summand. This matches "append `k` copies of `pred`".
nodes.rationale: The CMP(c)-augmented instance: original reports P plus k copies of the prediction; matches the displayed definition of the CMP(c) mechanism.

nodes.name: consistency_guarantee
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem 3 (consistency guarantee of `CMP(c)`).**

For `q = 2` and arbitrary dimension `d ≥ 1`: whenever the prediction equals an
optimal facility `fstar` (i.e. `socialCost 2 P fstar = optSocialCost 2 P`),
every coordinate-wise median `m` of the `CMP(c)`-augmented instance
`(P, ⌊c·n⌋ copies of fstar)` has social cost on the original agents at most
`CG(c) · OPT₂(P)`.

The hypothesis `(⌊c·n⌋ : ℝ) = c·n` requires the number of prediction copies to be
integral. This is the paper's standing assumption (it "ignores non-integrality",
working with `c·n` copies as an integer / in the `n → ∞` regime). The bound is
genuinely FALSE for finite `n` with `⌊cn⌋ < cn`: the effective prediction weight
`⌊cn⌋/n < c` yields the strictly worse bound `CG(⌊cn⌋/n) > CG(c)`.

The general-position hypothesis `(hfstar : ∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j)` records the
paper's standing normalization that the optimal facility is in GENERAL POSITION
relative to the returned median (`approx.tex` line 9: the analysis normalizes to
`f_i > 0` coordinate-wise after translating the median to the origin). It is a
FAITHFUL statement fix, not a weakening: the bound's proof reflects each
coordinate by the sign of `fstar j − m j` and rescales so that the translated
optimum `fstar − m` becomes a strictly-positive unit vector, which is exactly the
`f > 0` hypothesis required by the core inequality
`CGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`. (The ε-device that would relax this to
`fstar j ≠ 0`-only / `f ≥ 0` provably fails for the consistency core, because the
augmented median is `f`-dependent — see `proving_notes.md`.) Coordinates with
`fstar j = m j` contribute `0` to the optimum and to every `Δ_X = ∑_{j∈X} f_j²`,
so requiring them to be absent costs no generality in the paper's argument.
nodes.rationale: Theorem 3 (thm:consistency_guarantee): for q=2 and arbitrary d, when prediction equals the optimal facility, CMP(c) achieves social cost <= CG(c)*OPT. This is the full theorem statement.

nodes.name: lower_bound_tight
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem 2 (tightness / lower bound).**

The upper bound `UB q` of Theorem 1 cannot be improved. For every `q ≥ 1`
and every `ε > 0`, there is a placement instance `P : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ`
(with dimension `d ≥ 1`) whose coordinate-wise median is the zero vector,
whose optimal social cost is strictly positive, and whose median social cost
`socialCost q P 0` is at least `(UB q − ε) · optSocialCost q P`.

Combined with Theorem 1's `socialCost q P m ≤ UB q * optSocialCost q P`,
this pins the worst-case approximation ratio of the coordinate-wise median
mechanism at exactly `UB q`.
nodes.rationale: Theorem (thm:LB): for every q>=1 and eps>0 there is an instance whose coordinate-wise median is 0 with positive optimum, achieving social cost >= (UB q - eps)*OPT, i.e. the UB(q) upper bound is tight as d->infinity.

nodes.name: main_theorem
nodes.docstring:
**Main Theorem (Approximation guarantees of the coordinate-wise Median
Mechanism in `ℝ^d`).**

There exists a function `UB : ℝ → ℝ` (whose values for `q ≥ 1` are the
quantitatively-meaningful approximation factors) such that:

1. **(Approximation guarantee.)** For every `q ≥ 1`, every dimension
   `d ≥ 1`, every number of agents `n` (`n` is allowed to be `0`, in which
   case the bound is vacuous since both sides are `0`), every placement
   `P : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ`, and every coordinate-wise median `m` of `P`,
   `socialCost q P m ≤ UB q * optSocialCost q P`.
2. **(Base case.)** `UB 1 = 1`.
3. **(Limit at infinity.)** `UB q → 3` as `q → +∞`.
4. **(Euclidean case.)** `UB 2 = √(6√3 − 8)`.
nodes.rationale: Headline upper-bound theorem (Theorem thm:UB): social cost <= UB(q)*OPT, with UB(1)=1, UB->3, UB(2)=sqrt(6 sqrt 3 - 8).

nodes.name: CGABranchComparison_iff
nodes.docstring:
**CGABranchComparison** (prediction.tex line 197; appendix `a₁'` vs `(1-c)/2`).
For `c ≥ 0`, with `a₁' = (2 + c − √(3+2c))/2 = a1' c`:
`a₁' ≤ (1-c)/2 ⟺ c ≤ 1/2`.
(Proof: `a₁' − (1-c)/2 = (1 + 2c − √(3+2c))/2`, so the inequality is
`√(3+2c) ≥ 1 + 2c`; squaring both nonnegative sides gives
`0 ≥ 2(2c−1)(c+1) ⟺ c ≤ 1/2`.)
nodes.rationale: The branch-selection comparison a'_1 <= (1-c)/2 iff c <= 1/2 that decides whether the consistency optimum a_1 is the interior root (2+c-sqrt(3+2c))/2 or the boundary (1-c)/2 (consistency appendix). Proof-step link, lower confidence.

nodes.name: CGConstrainedMinExists
nodes.docstring:
**CGConstrainedMinExists** (proof_nlp.md §2.0–§2.1, `prediction.tex` line 38;
consistency analog of Theorem-1's `ConstrainedMinExists`, Claim 1).

Fix `q = 2` and `λ₁ = lambda1 c ∈ (0,1)`.  In the normalized setting
(`f j ≥ 0`, `‖f‖₂ = 1`), the minimum of `∑ᵢ g_lambda 2 λ₁ f (pᵢ)` over the
signature-fixed orthant — but now with the *consistency* orthant constraint
`∑ᵢ σ(pᵢ) j = −⌊cn⌋` (the output of `CGMedianConstraintFromAugment`) in place of
Theorem-1's `∑ᵢ σ(pᵢ) j = 0` — is attained.

This is the exact analog of `ConstrainedMinExists`: the only change to the
signature is the `hsigma_zero` hypothesis, which becomes the consistency form
`∀ j, ∑ i, sigma_assign i j = -(⌊c * n⌋₊ : ℝ)`.  (The orthant set is determined
by the per-coordinate signs `σ i j ∈ {−1,+1}` exactly as before; the constraint
on the *column sums* only restricts which `σ` arises, not the orthant geometry,
so the compactness/coercivity existence argument is unchanged.)
nodes.rationale: Existence/attainment of the constrained minimum for the consistency optimization (analog of Claim cl:compact set, but the paper only states the compact-set claim for the unconstrained main problem eq:main, not the consistency variant). Well-posedness plumbing, not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: CGDeltaLambdaHighBranch
nodes.docstring:
**CGDeltaLambdaHighBranch** (prediction.tex line 92; appendix.tex 215–220).
For `c ∈ [1/2, 1)`, with `a₁ = (1-c)/2` (so the term `(1−2a₁−c)/(1+c)` vanishes
since `1 − 2a₁ − c = 0`), the value `δ₁²` obtained from `u₁(a₁) = 0` is
`δ₁² = a₁/(1−a₁) = ((1-c)/2)/((1+c)/2) = (1-c)/(1+c)`, and the resulting
`λ₁ = (1 + δ₁²)^{-1/2} = (2/(1+c))^{-1/2} = √((c+1)/2)`, so
`1/λ₁ = √(2/(c+1)) = CG c`.

We state: on this branch the closed-form `lambda1 c` (defined as `√((c+1)/2)`)
satisfies the chain of equalities
`δ₁² = (1-c)/(1+c)`, `lambda1 c = (1 + δ₁²)^{-1/2} = √((c+1)/2)`, and
`1 / lambda1 c = CG c`.
nodes.rationale: High branch c in [1/2,1): with a1=(1-c)/2 the term (1-2a1-c) vanishes, delta1^2 = (1-c)/(1+c) and lambda1 = sqrt((c+1)/2). This is the c>=1/2 branch closed-form derivation of lambda_1 in the appendix proof of thm:consistency_guarantee; 1/lambda1 = CG c = sqrt(2/(c+1)). Linked to the precise appendix block (proof step).

nodes.name: CGEvenAugmentReduction
nodes.docstring:
**CGEvenAugmentReduction** (prediction.tex 188–208; consistency analog of
`ReductionToEvenN`).

To prove the consistency bound for every instance (with an integral number of
prediction copies, `⌊cn⌋ = cn`), it SUFFICES to prove it for instances in which
the augmented size `n + ⌊cn⌋` is even. The reduction is by duplicating the entire
original instance `P` to `2n`: this doubles both `socialCost 2 P m` and
`optSocialCost 2 P` (so the ratio is unchanged), keeps `m` a coordinate-wise
median of the augmented instance, and — because `⌊cn⌋ = cn` makes
`⌊c·2n⌋ = 2⌊cn⌋` — makes the new augmented size `2n + ⌊c·2n⌋ = 2(n + ⌊cn⌋)` even.

The integral-prediction-count hypothesis `(⌊cn⌋ : ℝ) = cn` is the paper's standing
assumption (it "ignores non-integrality"); it is carried by both the `h_even`
premise and the conclusion so that the doubled instance — which still has an
integral count, `⌊c·2n⌋ = c·2n` — satisfies the premise.
nodes.rationale: Demoted to helper: proof-machinery/sub-expression/duplicate on a proof-prose anchor; the stating decl keeps the link (was: Demoted to helper: proof-machinery/sub-expression/duplicate on a proof-prose anchor; the stating decl keeps the link (was: WLOG even-size reduction (consistency analog): it suffices to prove the consistency bound for instances whose augmented size n+floor(cn) is even, justified by duplicating all points. The paper makes this even-n normalization explicitly only for the base median analysis (quoted); the consistency proof inherits it implicitly. Low-confidence proof-step link.))

nodes.name: CGFinalAssembly
nodes.docstring:
**CGFinalAssembly** — the proof of Theorem 3 (consistency guarantee of
`CMP(c)`), assembled from the consistency sub-lemmas.

This is the body of `Workspace.ConsistencyTheorem.consistency_guarantee`; the
root statement file sets `consistency_guarantee := CGFinalAssembly`.

Pipeline (proof_nlp.md §1.2, §7):
* `CGEvenAugmentReduction` reduces to the case `n + ⌊cn⌋` even (and discharges
  `n = 0`) by duplicating the augmented instance.
* In the even case we split on `optSocialCost 2 P = 0`:
  - `OPT = 0`: every report equals the optimal facility, the augmented instance
    is the constant `fstar`, its median is `fstar`, so `SC(P,m) = 0 ≤ CG c · 0`.
  - `OPT > 0`: `CGTranslationScaleNormalize` (its `h_norm` premise instantiated
    with the strict-`f>0` core `CGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`) gives the bound,
    using the general-position hypothesis `∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j` to certify that the
    reflected/normalized optimum is strictly positive coordinate-wise.

The general-position hypothesis is the paper's standing normalization
(`approx.tex` line 9); see `consistency_guarantee`'s docstring.
nodes.rationale: The proof body of Theorem 3 (consistency guarantee); the root statement file sets consistency_guarantee := CGFinalAssembly. Same statement as the consistency theorem.

nodes.name: CGLambda1InUnitInterval
nodes.docstring:
**CGLambda1InUnitInterval** (prediction.tex 89–95; proof_nlp.md §5.5).
For every `c ∈ [0,1)`, the constant `λ₁ = lambda1 c` given by the two-branch
closed form satisfies `0 < λ₁ ∧ λ₁ < 1`; equivalently `CG c = 1/λ₁ > 1`.

* For `c < 1/2`: `4√(2c+3)c + 6√(2c+3) − 10c − 8 > (c+1)² > 0` (e.g. at `c = 0`,
  `6√3 − 8 > 1`, the `SixSqrtThreeMinusEightPos`-style bound), so `λ₁ < 1`.
* For `c ≥ 1/2`: `λ₁ = √((c+1)/2)` with `(c+1)/2 > 0` and `(c+1)/2 < 1 ⟺ c < 1`.

We state both `0 < λ₁ < 1` and `1 < CG c`.
nodes.rationale: 0 < lambda1 c < 1 and CG c = 1/lambda1 > 1 for c in [0,1): establishes that the closed-form lambda_1 (the two-branch expression in the consistency proof) is a genuine relaxation multiplier in (0,1), so CG(c)=1/lambda_1 is a valid (>1) consistency ratio. Range/validity step for the lambda_1 closed form.

nodes.name: CGMedianConstraintFromAugment
nodes.docstring:
**CGMedianConstraintFromAugment** (prediction.tex line 30, `eq:consistency
main`; consistency analog of `MedianConstraintFromCWMedian`).  Gap (i).

Normalized setting: `m = 0`, `f j > 0` for all `j`, `‖f‖₂ = 1` (i.e.
`∑ⱼ (fⱼ)² = 1`), and `n + ⌊cn⌋` even.  If `0` is a coordinate-wise median of
`augment P f ⌊cn⌋` (the instance `P` with `⌊cn⌋` extra agents all at `f`), then
there is a signature assignment `σ : Fin n → Fin d → {−1,+1}` consistent with the
signs of `P` such that for every coordinate `j`,
`∑_{i∈[n]} σ(pᵢ) j = −⌊cn⌋`.
Equivalently, for every `j`, `#{i : σⱼ(pᵢ) = +1} = (n − ⌊cn⌋)/2`.
nodes.rationale: The median-at-0 constraint of the augmented (CMP) instance is sum_i sigma(p_i) = -cn, the constraint of eq:consistency main.

nodes.name: CGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos
nodes.docstring:
The `f > 0` (strictly positive) version of `CGNormalizedCoreInequality`
(consistency analog of `NormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`, at `q = 2`).

This carries the paper's normalization hypothesis `hf_pos : ∀ j, 0 < f j`,
required by `LocalOptimumCharacterization` / `GLambdaLowerBound_h`.  In the
normalized setting (`m = 0`, the prediction equals the normalized minimizer `f`
with all-positive coordinates and `‖f‖₂ = 1`), if `0` is a coordinate-wise
median of the *augmented* instance `augment P_norm f ⌊cn⌋` and `n + ⌊cn⌋` is
even, then `SC(P_norm, 0) ≤ CG c · SC(P_norm, f)`.

(Its eventual proof assembles `CGMedianConstraintFromAugment` →
`CGConstrainedMinExists` → `GLambdaLowerBound_h` (external) → `CGRelaxedConstraint`
→ `CGRelaxedCoreNonneg` → `CGLambda1InUnitInterval`, exactly mirroring
`NormalizedCoreInequality_fpos` with `UB 2` replaced by `CG c`, the median-of-`P`
hypothesis replaced by median-of-augmented, the even-`n` hypothesis replaced by
`Even (n + ⌊cn⌋)`, and the constraint `∑ x = n/2` replaced by `∑ x = (1-c)/2·n`.)
nodes.rationale: Strict-positivity (f_j>0) version of the consistency normalized core inequality: socialCost 2 P 0 <= CG c * cost(f). This realizes, lifted back to social cost, the consistency relaxed-optimization problem (the displayed min sum h(x_i) s.t. sum x_i = (1-c)/2 n). Fine-grained core proof step of Theorem (consistency).

nodes.name: CGRelaxedConstraint
nodes.docstring:
**CGRelaxedConstraint** (prediction.tex 48–54, `eq: consistency
relaxed_median_constraint`; consistency analog of `MedianConstraintToSumX`).
Gap (ii).

In the normalized setting (`f j > 0`, `∑ⱼ (fⱼ)² = 1`), with the signature `σ` of
`CGMedianConstraintFromAugment` — so for each coordinate `j` exactly
`(n − ⌊cn⌋)/2` of the original agents have `σⱼ(pᵢ) = +1` — and
`xᵢ := Δ_{S(pᵢ)} = ∑_{j : σⱼ(pᵢ)=1} (fⱼ)²`, one has
`∑_{i∈[n]} xᵢ = (1−c)/2 · n`.

(Proof: swap the order of summation; `∑ᵢ xᵢ = ∑ⱼ (fⱼ)² · #{i : j∈S(pᵢ)}
= ∑ⱼ (fⱼ)² · (n − cn)/2 = (1−c)/2 · n · ∑ⱼ (fⱼ)² = (1−c)/2 · n`.)

We take the per-coordinate balance count as a hypothesis (the conclusion of
`CGMedianConstraintFromAugment`), written real-valued as
`#{i : σⱼ = 1} = (n − ⌊cn⌋)/2`.
nodes.rationale: The consistency relaxed median constraint: in the normalized setting sum_i x_i = (1-c)/2 * n. This is exactly the displayed chain of equalities (eq: consistency relaxed_median_constraint).

nodes.name: tangent_below_convex_concave
nodes.docstring:
**Tangent-below bound for a convex-then-concave function.**  If `f` is convex on
`[0,z]` and concave on `[z,1]`, `a ∈ (0,z]`, and `f` has derivative `D` at `a`, then for
all `y ∈ [0,1]`, `f y ≥ f a + D·(y − a)` — the global tangent at `a` lies below `f`.
(Convexity gives it on `[0,z]`; on `[z,1]` the tangent line is `≤` the chord from
`(z,f z)` to `(1,f 1)` since it is `≤ f` at both endpoints, and the chord is `≤ f` by
concavity.)
nodes.rationale: Generic convex-then-concave tangent-below lemma; abstract analytic tool, not a paper statement.

nodes.name: CGTranslationScaleNormalize
nodes.docstring:
**CGTranslationScaleNormalize** (proof_nlp.md §1.2, §7; consistency analog of
Theorem-1's `TranslationScaleNormalize`, at `q = 2`).

Given the consistency normalized core inequality `h_norm` in its `f > 0` (strict
general-position) form — the conclusion of `CGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`: for
the augmented median at `0`, `‖f‖₂ = 1`, `f ≥ 0` AND `f > 0`, `n + ⌊cn⌋` even,
`SC(P_norm,0) ≤ CG c · SC(P_norm,f)` — the general consistency bound holds for an
arbitrary instance `P` with optimal facility `fstar` IN GENERAL POSITION relative
to the returned median (`∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j`), `SC(P,fstar) = OPT(P)`,
`OPT(P) > 0`, `n + ⌊cn⌋` even, and any coordinate-wise median `m` of the augmented
instance `augment P fstar ⌊cn⌋`: `SC(P,m) ≤ CG c · OPT(P)`.

The reduction (translation by `m`, sign-reflection so `fstar − m ≥ 0`
coordinate-wise, and positive scaling so `‖fstar − m‖₂ = 1`) preserves both the
augmented coordinate-median property at `0` — because the `⌊cn⌋` prediction
copies sit at `fstar` and move with it — and the ratio `SC(P,m)/OPT(P)`, exactly
as `TranslationScaleNormalize` does for Theorem 1.

**Why the strict `f > 0` form (and the general-position `∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j`).**
The ε-perturbation device that would let the `f ≥ 0` core suffice provably fails
for the consistency analysis, because the augmented median hypothesis is
`f`-dependent (the prediction copies sit at `f`), so perturbing `f` can break the
median property — see `proving_notes.md`. The faithful route is therefore the
strict core `CGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`, which requires `f > 0`.  Under the
reflection normalization the translated optimum is `v_refl j = eps j · (fstar j −
m j) = |fstar j − m j|`, which is `> 0` for every `j` precisely because
`fstar j ≠ m j`; after scaling by `σ = 1/‖v_refl‖₂ > 0` the normalized optimum
`f_norm` is strictly positive coordinate-wise, supplying the `hf_pos` argument of
`h_norm`.  The `Even (n + ⌊cn⌋)` hypothesis is supplied upstream by
`CGEvenAugmentReduction`.

**RGFinalAssembly** — the proof of Theorem 4 (robustness guarantee of
`CMP(c)`), assembled from the robustness sub-lemmas.

This is the body of `Workspace.RobustnessTheorem.robustness_guarantee`; the
root statement file sets `robustness_guarantee := RGFinalAssembly`.

Pipeline (faithful `c → −c` / `fstar → pred` mirror of `CGFinalAssembly`):
* `RGEvenAugmentReduction` reduces to the case `n + ⌊cn⌋` even (and discharges
  `n = 0`) by duplicating the pred-augmented instance.
* In the even case we split on `optSocialCost 2 P = 0`:
  - `OPT = 0`: every report equals the optimal facility `fstar'`, so the
    pred-augmented instance is `fstar'` on the `n'` agents and `pred'` on the
    `⌊cn'⌋` appended copies.  Because `⌊cn'⌋ < n'`, the original agents form a
    STRICT majority on every coordinate, so any median `m'` equals `fstar'`
    (`strictMajority_median_eq`).  Then `SC(P',m') = SC(P',fstar') = 0 ≤ RG c · 0`.
  - `OPT > 0`: `RGTranslationScaleNormalize` (its `h_norm` premise instantiated
    with the strict-`f>0` core `RGNormalizedCoreInequality_fpos`) gives the bound,
    using the general-position hypotheses `∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j` and `∀ j, pred j ≠ m j`.

The general-position hypotheses are the paper's standing normalization; see
`robustness_guarantee`'s docstring.
nodes.rationale: The proof body of Theorem 4 (robustness guarantee of CMP(c)): SC(P,m) <= RG(c)*OPT for any coordinate median of the pred-augmented instance. The root statement file sets robustness_guarantee := RGFinalAssembly.

nodes.name: RG
nodes.docstring:
The closed-form robustness bound `RG(c)` for the `CMP(c)` mechanism at
`q = 2` (Euclidean L₂), from Theorem 4 of Gravin & Jia.

`RG(c) = 1/λ₂ = √(−4·√(3−2c)·c + 6·√(3−2c) + 10c − 8) / (1 − c)`,  `c ∈ [0,1)`.

Unlike consistency's `CG(c)`, the robustness `RG(c)` has a **single branch**
across the whole interval `c ∈ [0,1)`: the interior root
`a₂' = (2−c−√(3−2c))/2 ≤ (1+c)/2` for every `c ∈ [0,1)`, so the boundary case
`a₂ = (1+c)/2` never binds (appendix.tex lines 310–311). There is NO `if c < 1/2`
split here, in contrast to the two-branch `CG`.

(The `^{1/2}` in the paper is rendered with `Real.sqrt`.)
nodes.rationale: Closed-form robustness bound RG(c) for CMP(c) at q=2, the displayed expression of Theorem thm:robustness_guarantee.

nodes.name: robustness_guarantee
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem 4 (robustness guarantee of `CMP(c)`).**

For `q = 2` and arbitrary dimension `d ≥ 1`: for EVERY prediction `pred ∈ ℝ^d`,
every coordinate-wise median `m` of the `CMP(c)`-augmented instance
`(P, ⌊c·n⌋ copies of pred)` has social cost on the original agents at most
`RG(c) · OPT₂(P)`. Robustness is the WORST case over ALL predictions: the extra
universal binder `∀ (pred : Fin d → ℝ)` is the only structural difference from the
consistency theorem (Theorem 3), which fixes `pred = fstar`. Here `pred` is
arbitrary while `fstar` remains an optimal facility — it defines `optSocialCost`
and the general-position condition. The bound holds for every prediction because
the worst-case prediction (signature `(−1,…,−1)`) already attains the maximum
`RG(c)`, and every other prediction gives a value `≤ RG(c)`.

The hypothesis `(⌊c·n⌋ : ℝ) = c·n` requires the number of prediction copies to be
integral. This is the paper's standing assumption (it "ignores non-integrality",
working with `c·n` copies as an integer / in the `n → ∞` regime) — the SAME
faithful fix as in consistency (Theorem 3).

The general-position hypothesis `(hgp : ∀ j, fstar j ≠ m j)` records the paper's
standing normalization that the optimal facility is in GENERAL POSITION relative
to the returned median (`approx.tex` line 9: the analysis normalizes to `f_i > 0`
coordinate-wise after translating the median to the origin). It is the SAME
faithful statement fix as in consistency (Theorem 3) — see the
`consistency_guarantee` docstring and `theorem_robustness_text.md`: the bound's
proof reflects each coordinate by the sign of `fstar j − m j` and rescales so that
the translated optimum becomes a strictly-positive unit vector. Coordinates with
`fstar j = m j` contribute `0` to the optimum and to every `Δ_X = ∑_{j∈X} f_j²`,
so requiring them absent costs no generality.

Like `fstar`, the prediction `pred` is assumed in general position relative to the
returned median (`hgp_pred : ∀ j, pred j ≠ m j`): the worst-case-prediction
analysis (`prediction.tex` Lemma `lm:optimal solution for sigma(pred)`) ranges over
predictions with a DEFINITE signature `σ(pred) ∈ {±1}^d` — i.e. `pred_j ≠ m_j` after
translating the median to the origin — so a degenerate `pred_j = m_j` lies outside
the paper's argument. This is the exact analog of the `fstar` general-position fix.
nodes.rationale: For q=2 and arbitrary d, for EVERY prediction pred, CMP(c) achieves social cost <= RG(c)*OPT. Exactly the robustness-guarantee theorem (worst case over all predictions).

nodes.name: IsCoordinateMedian
nodes.docstring:
A vector `m : Fin d → ℝ` is a *coordinate-wise median* of the instance
`P : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ` if for every coordinate `j`, both the number of
indices `i` with `P i j < m j` and the number of indices with
`P i j > m j` are at most `n / 2` (natural-number integer division).

When `n` is even, this gives `n / 2` on each side; when `n` is odd, this
gives `⌊n/2⌋ = (n - 1) / 2` on each side. The predicate models arbitrary
tie-breaking: many `m` will satisfy it for typical instances.
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the coordinate-wise median mechanism: m_j is the median of the j-th coordinates. The relational predicate (at most n/2 strictly above/below each coordinate) captures the tie-breaking footnote.

We avoid `PiLp` / `EuclideanSpace` so the formula textually matches the
paper. The dimension `d` is implicit; the function is total in `q : ℝ`,
but the meaningful basic properties (non-negativity, scaling by a real)
are stated with `1 ≤ q` as required.

nodes.name: optSocialCost
nodes.docstring: The optimal social cost is the infimum over all facility locations.
nodes.rationale: Optimal social cost = infimum over facility locations of SC; the paper writes it inline as SC(locs, f^*). Lower conf as it is not a separately named object.

nodes.name: optSocialCost_le_socialCost
nodes.docstring:
The optimal social cost is a lower bound for the social cost at every
facility location (under `1 ≤ q`, which gives `BddBelow`).
nodes.rationale: OPT is a lower bound for cost at any facility; basic infimum property.

nodes.name: optSocialCost_nonneg
nodes.docstring: The optimal social cost is non-negative under `1 ≤ q`.
nodes.rationale: Non-negativity of optimal social cost; infrastructure.

nodes.name: socialCost
nodes.docstring:
The social cost of placing a facility at `f : Fin d → ℝ` for `n`
agents whose preferred locations are the rows of `P : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ`,
measured under the `L_q` norm:
`socialCost q P f = ∑_{i=1}^n lqNorm q (p_i − f)`,
where `(p_i − f) j = P i j − f j`.
nodes.rationale: Definition of social cost SC(P,f) = sum_i ||f - p_i||_q.

nodes.name: socialCost_bddBelow
nodes.docstring:
The set of social costs (over all facility locations) is bounded below
by `0` whenever `1 ≤ q`.
nodes.rationale: Bounded-below fact needed so the infimum optSocialCost is well-defined; infrastructure.

nodes.name: socialCost_empty_agents
nodes.docstring:
With zero agents the social cost is `0` for every facility location
and every `q`.
nodes.rationale: Edge case (zero agents => cost 0); infrastructure.

nodes.name: socialCost_nonneg
nodes.docstring: The social cost is non-negative whenever `1 ≤ q`.
nodes.rationale: Basic non-negativity of social cost; not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: perPointCount
nodes.docstring:
Per-point count: for a fixed cyclic shift `s`, exactly `kCount q d` coordinates
are active for a Type-I point (the length-`k` cyclic block, when `k < d`). This is
the per-POINT analogue of `LBIntegrality`'s per-coordinate balancedness count, proved
by the same cyclic-rotation bijection.
nodes.rationale: Per-point combinatorial count (exactly k active coordinates per Type-I point); helper for LBSocialCosts, not separately stated.
